title: Generic constancy of geometric connected-component counts
statement: Let $f:Y\to T$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For $t\in T$, let $n_f(t)\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ be the well-defined geometric connected-component count of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change]: the number of maximal nonempty connected subsets of $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K$ for an algebraically closed extension $K$ of the residue field $\kappa(t)$, with infinite counts recorded as $\infty$ and the empty fibre having count $0$. For every nonempty irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq|T|$, there are a nonempty relatively open subset $V\subseteq Z$ and a value $c\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ such that $n_f(t)=c$ for every $t\in V$. Here irreducible means that any two nonempty relatively open subsets intersect. No finite-presentation, flatness, smoothness, properness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 055H, label lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-good; reformulated for irreducible closed subsets Z, each of which is the closure of its generic point in a scheme (Schemes Tag 01IS, lemma-scheme-sober). Counts are those of Tag 055F.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq|T|$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], $Z=\overline{\{\eta\}}$ for a generic point $\eta$. Give $Z$ its reduced induced closed scheme structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The base change $X=Y\times_T Z\to Z$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], and [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change] identifies its count function with $n_f|_Z$. It suffices to find a nonempty open in this irreducible base on which its count is constant. Rename this morphism $h:X\to S$.

source.place: Tag 055H, first paragraph; scheme sobriety is Tag 01IS.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-etale-generic-component-splitting] to $h$. It gives an irreducible affine $B$ and a finite etale surjection $g:B\to U$ onto a nonempty open of $S$. Put $q:P=X\times_S B\to B$ and write $\xi$ for the generic point of $B$. Base-change stability makes $q$ finite type. Every irreducible component of $G=P_\xi$ is geometrically irreducible. We will find an open neighbourhood of $\xi$ in $B$ with constant geometric count and then take its open image in $S$.

The fibre $G$ is finite type over the field $k=\kappa(\xi)$ by base change. A field has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, so it is Noetherian and its one-point spectrum is a Noetherian scheme. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $G$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components] and [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], its irreducible components form a finite closed cover $(A_i)_{i\in I}$. The index set $I$ is finite, and $I$ is empty exactly when $G$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 055H, final paragraph, finite generic component decomposition; Tag 01T6 for the Noetherian fibre.

proof.text: Join $i,j\in I$ by an edge when $A_i\cap A_j\ne\varnothing$. Each $A_i$ is connected: a separation would contradict irreducibility. The union belonging to a graph component is connected, since a separation cannot split a vertex or two intersecting vertices, hence cannot split a path. Different graph-component unions are disjoint, and each is closed, being a finite union of closed $A_i$; its complement is also closed. These nonempty clopen connected unions are therefore exactly the connected components of $G$ (a nonempty clopen connected subset is a maximal connected subset). Let $n$ be the number of graph components, a finite integer since $I$ is finite; then $G$ has exactly $n$ connected components. If $I$ is empty, $n=0$ and $G$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 055G, final paragraph (equivalence classes of the intersection relation), as used for Tag 055H; this step defines the finite integer $n$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-geometric-generic-cover-spread] to $q$, with $L=k$, the identity finite etale spectrum map and the supplied cover $(A_i)$. The geometric-irreducibility hypothesis is Step 2. Obtain an open $W_+\ni\xi$ such that for every $b\in W_+$ and every field extension $K/\kappa(b)$ there is a surjection $p:Q\to P_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and a cover $(D_i)$ of $Q$ by nonempty irreducible subsets, preserving every edge of the generic intersection graph. For each of its $n$ graph components, the corresponding union of the $D_i$ is connected by the separation-and-path argument of Step 4. Its image under $p$ is connected: a separation pulls back to a separation of that union. The $n$ images cover the target by surjectivity, so the target has at most $n$ connected components: each nonempty connected image lies in one maximal component, and every target point belongs to an image. This uses [lem-sfb-connected-component-maximality]. When $n=0$, the empty cover forces $Q$, and hence the target, to be empty. In particular $n_q(b)\le n$ on $W_+$.

source.place: Tag 055H, upper-bound part of final paragraph, using the geometric closed-cover and intersection-spreading construction of Tag 055G.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-generic-connected-component-lower-bound] to $q$ with the integer $n$ of Step 4, the number of connected components of $G=P_\xi$. It gives an open $W_-\ni\xi$ on which every ordinary fibre $P_b$ has at least $n$ connected components. For any algebraically closed extension $K/\kappa(b)$, [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] make $P_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K\to P_b$ surjective. A continuous surjection cannot decrease the number of connected components in its source: the image of each source component is connected (pull back a separation), lies in a single target component by [lem-sfb-connected-component-maximality], and every target component is hit. Thus $n_q(b)\ge n$. Combining with Step 5 gives $n_q=n$ on the nonempty open $W=W_-\cap W_+$.

source.place: Tag 055H, lower-bound part of final paragraph, using Tag 055D; comparison of ordinary and geometric components via the field-extension projection.

proof.text: The etale map $g$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], so $V=g(W)$ is a nonempty open subset of $U$, hence of $S$. For $s\in V$, choose $b\in W$ with $g(b)=s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change], $n_h(s)=n_q(b)=n$. Step 1 identifies this $V$ with a nonempty relatively open subset of the original $Z$ and identifies the count there with $n_f$. Take $c=n$. All base changes were unrestricted, and no additional hypothesis was imposed on the original family.

source.place: Tag 055H, open-image descent in paragraph 2; the count identity is Tag 055F (not the irreducible-component count identity).

proof_origin.place: Tag 055H (lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-good), with the finite generic irreducible-cover form of the upper-bound argument from Tag 055G and the ordinary lower bound of Tag 055D.
